title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
subtitle: Sharp and sweet loaf cake
excerpt: A moist, tender lemon loaf cake soaked in a sharp lemon syrup while still warm, which sets to a slightly crunchy crust. The drizzle is what makes it.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lemon drizzle cake is a modern British baking classic, frequently cited as one of the most popular cakes in the UK. The sharp lemon syrup poured over the warm cake while still in the tin was popularised by Delia Smith in the 1970s.

recipeTools.notes: A standard 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
For creaming the butter and sugar.

content.text: Lemon drizzle cake is a lemon sponge loaf soaked with sharp lemon syrup while still warm. The syrup soaks into the crumb and leaves a lightly crunchy sugar crust on top. The flavour intensifies as it sits, so it is often better the day after baking.

items.preparation: zest of both, juice for the drizzle

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease a 900 g loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Beat the butter and 175 g caster sugar together for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating between each. Stir in the lemon zest.
Fold in the flour and milk until the batter is smooth. Pour into the prepared tin and smooth the top.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and the top is golden.
While the cake bakes, stir the lemon juice and the 80 g caster sugar together in a small bowl. Do not heat it; the sugar will not fully dissolve, which is correct.

As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, prick it all over with a skewer or fork while still in the tin. Spoon the lemon drizzle slowly over the top so it soaks in. Leave in the tin until completely cool before lifting out.
